the 3xTG-AD mice exhibit a spatial working memory deficit at 3 months of age, which coincides with a reduction in the NMDA-dependent component of hippocampal synaptic plasticity.

the early onset of spatial working memory deficits in the 3Xtg-AD mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease is associated with a reduction of the NMDA-receptor dependent component of hippocampal LTP and a concomitant increase in the non NMDAR component of LTP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between synaptic dysfunction and cognitive deficits in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease.
the relationship between synaptic plasticity and memory function in the 3 x transgenic AD mouse model.
how alterations in synaptic plastic mechanisms may contribute to the onset of Alzheimer's disease and its associated cognitive deficits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the onset of cognitive deficits in the 3×Tg AD mouse occurs before the onset of amyloid beta plaques and tau pathology, and that this deficit is associated with alterations in synaptic plastic mechanisms that are dependent on NMDA receptor function.
the onset of the cognitive impairment and the accompanying alterations in synaptic plastic are not directly related to the formation of plaques and/or tangles.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the onset of Alzheimer's disease occurs before amyloid plaque and tangle formation and that the onset of this disease is characterized by deficits in spatial working and alterations in synaptic plastic.
the 3x Tg-AD mouse model is useful for studying the onset of cognitive deficits and associated synaptic plasticity alterations in a pre-symptomatic model of Alzheimer's.
the early presence of cognitive impairment in the 3 xTg AD mice may be related to the early alterations in synaptic plastic.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3xTG AD mouse is a good model for studying early stage Alzheimer's disease, and that the 3 month old 3xTG mice are impaired in spatial working memory and have alterations in synaptic plastic that correlate with these deficits.
the 3xTG AD mouse model is an ideal model for studying the earliest stages of the disease.
